Kırklareli Province (Turkish: Kırklareli ili) is a province in northwestern Turkey on the west coast of the Black Sea. The province neighbours Bulgaria to the north along a 180-kilometre (110 mi) long border. It borders the province of Edirne to the west, the province of Tekirdağ to the south, and the province of Istanbul to the southeast. Kırklareli is the capital city of the province. Its area is 6,459 km2, and its population is 369,347 (2022). 
The province's and its central city's name means "the land of the forties" in Turkish and it may refer either to the forty Ottoman ghazis sent by the sultan Murad I to conquer the city for the Ottoman Empire in the 14th century or to the forty churches reported to be situated in the region before the Ottoman conquest, as attested by the former name of Kırklareli (Kırk Kilise in Turkish; Σαράντα Εκκλησιές). There is a memorial on a hilltop in Kırklareli city, called "Kırklar Anıtı" (the Memorial of the Forties in Turkish) to honor the Ottoman conquerors (For more on the name's origins, see Kırklareli). The province is bisected by the Yıldız (Istranca) mountain range. The north and northeastern parts of the province are among the least populated and under developed parts of Turkey. The districts to the south and west are more populated because the land is better suited for agriculture and industrial development. The north and eastern parts of the province are dominated by forests. Therefore, forestry is an important means of living in these areas. Fishing is done along the Black Sea coast.

Q3658667: The Dupnisa Cave (Turkish: Dupnisa Mağarası), aka Dupnisa Caves, is a show cave located in Kırklareli Province, northwestern Turkey, close to Bulgarian-Turkish border. The cave itself, unlike what the original name suggests, is actually three, interconnected caves divided into two separate floors. Its name is derived from the Bulgarian word Dupnitsa (Дупница), related to the word for "hole".
Q19931239:
The İğneada Floodplain Forests National Park (Turkish: İğneada Longoz Ormanları Milli Parkı), established on November 13, 2007, is a national park located within Kırklareli Province in Marmara region at East Thrace, the European part of Turkey.
The national park covers an area of 3,155 ha (7,800 acres) and is located at İğneada town on the Turkish-Bulgarian border at 25 km (16 mi) far from Demirköy District of Kırklareli Province.
Streams running down from the Strandzha mountain range towards Black Sea formed alluvium on the shore, where floodplain (Turkish: longoz) occurred due to seasonal floodings.
The protected area is administered by the Directorate-General of Nature Protection and National Parks (Turkish: Doğa Koruma ve Milli Parklar Genel Müdürlüğü) of the Ministry of Environment and Forest.
The national park is a rare ecosystem, which consists of marsh, swamp, lakes and coastal sand dunes. The Strandzha mountain range is situated in the south and west. There are five lakes with aquatic plant. Lake Erikli covering 43 ha (110 acres) is a lagoon, which gets separated from the sea in the summer months as a result of drought. Lake Mert of 266 ha (660 acres) area is formed by Çavuşdere creek at its mouth. Lake Saka is a small lake of 5 ha (12 acres) situated in the south of the national park between the floodplain and the dunes. The two other lakes are Lake Hamam of size 19 ha (47 acres) and Lake Pedina of 10 ha (25 acres). The sand dunes are situated on both sides of İğneada town. The dunes in the north stretch out from east of Lake Erikli to İğneada.
Q20988467: Kırklareli Museum (Turkish: Kırklareli Müzesi) is a national museum in Kırklareli, Turkey, exhibiting natural history specimens, ethnographical items related to the region's history of cultural life, and archaeological artifacts found in and around the city. The director of the museum is Derya Balkan.
Q52790862: Gazi Süleyman Pasha Mosque, or Little Hagia Sophia, is a mosque in the Vize district of Kırklareli. It was built in the 6th century, under Emperor Justinian I, as a basilica-style church and is thought to have been converted into a mosque in the 15th century, after Vize came firmly under Ottoman rule. Its structure is compared to Hagia Sophia and Hagia Irene.
Q1402638:
Mount Mahya (Turkish: Mahya Dağı; Bulgarian: Махиада, romanized: Mahiada) (1031 m) is a mountain peak in Turkey. It is the highest peak of the Strandzha Massif (Yıldız Mountains) and also the European part of Turkey.
Mount Ararat is the highest point in Turkey as a whole.
Q38174028:
The Sokollu Mehmed Pasha Mosque (Turkish: Sokollu Mehmet Paşa Camii) is a 16th-century Ottoman mosque located in the town of Lüleburgaz in the Kırklareli Province of northwestern Turkey.
The mosque was commissioned by the grand vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha (in office 1565–1579) and designed by the imperial architect Mimar Sinan. It was built between 1565 and 1569–70 and forms part of a large complex that includes a medrese (theological school), a hospice and a caravansarai.
Q102252123: İğneada Lighthouse is a lighthouse in the town of İğneada, Demirköy (Kırklareli).
Q20717664: The Demirköy Foundry (Turkish: Demirköy Dökümhanesi) is a historic foundry ruin of archaeological importance located at Demirköy in Kırklareli Province, northwestern Turkey.
Q6020905: The Monastery of St Nicholas (Aya Nikola) in Kıyıköy, Vize (Kırklareli), is one of the oldest rock-cut monasteries in the world.
Q126443534: Hızırbey Mosque Fountain, Great Mosque Fountain, German Fountain, or Çarşı Fountain, is a historical fountain located in the central district of Kırklareli, Turkey.
Q65051022:
Salmydessus or Salmydessos, also Halmydessus or Halmydissos (Ἁλμυδισσός), was a town on the Euxine Sea in ancient Thrace, about 97 kilometres (60 mi) northwest of the entrance of the Bosporus, near present day Kıyıköy in European Turkey. The eastern offshoots of the Haemus Mountains come very close to the shore here, which they divide from the valley of the Hebrus.
Little is known of the history of Salmydessus. Herodotus writes that "...before he [Darius the Great] came to the Ister, he first took the Getae, who pretend to be immortal. The Thracians of Salmydessus and of the country above the towns of Apollonia and Mesambria, who are called Cyrmianae and Nipsaei, surrendered without a fight to Darius; but the Getae resisted stubbornly, and were enslaved at once, the bravest and most just Thracians of all." During the reign of Seuthes II (c. 405 - 387 BCE) Xenophon and the remnants of his Ten Thousand took the town for the Thracian ruler. Xenophon writes that "...after subduing the country in this neighborhood," he and the remains of the Ten Thousand "set out upon their return." In the Dictionary of Greek and Roman Geography it is said that "...the earlier writers appear to speak of Salmydessus as a district only, but in later authors, as Apollodorus, Pliny, and Mela, it is mentioned as a town."
Xenophon describes the coast of the Euxine Sea along Salmydessus as having numerous shoals, making it a dangerous port for sailors.
Q127634992: Rüstem Pasha Mosque, or Cağaloğlu Rüstem Pasha Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in the town of Büyükkarıştıran, Lüleburgaz (Kırklareli). The original was built in the 17th century; it was destroyed during the Balkan Wars and rebuilt in 1937.
Q127786850: Kadı Ali Mosque, also called Gazi, Gazi Ali Bey, Eski or Kadı Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in the Lüleburgaz district of Kırklareli, opposite the Sokullu Mehmed Pasha Bridge.
Q127786852: Kadı Emin Ali Çelebi Mosque, also called Kadı, Emin Ali Çelebi or Küçük (Small) Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in central Kırklareli.
Q127788070: Semiz Ali Pasha Mosque, or Cedid Ali Pasha Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli, commissioned by Semiz Ali Pasha from Mimar Sinan.
Q130315985: Şerbetdar Hasan Bey Mosque, or Şarabdar Hasan Bey Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Vize district of Kırklareli.
Q132133895: Fatih Mosque, also called Eski or Küçük Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli. The Four-Sided Fountain and the Babaeski Bath stand in front of it.
Q132134113: Gülabi Ahmed Pasha Mosque, also called Paşa or Beyazıt Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in central Kırklareli.
Q132134114: Kapan Mosque, or Karaca İbrahim Bey Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in central Kırklareli.
Q133319341: Karakaş Bey Mosque, or Karakaş Mosque, is in central Kırklareli. The original Ottoman mosque was built in the 17th century; after it was destroyed at an unknown date it was rebuilt in reinforced concrete.
Q133864247: Fatma Hatun Mosque, or Fatma Hatun Mescidi, is in the Vize district of Kırklareli. The original small prayer house is said to date from the first half of the 17th century; local residents rebuilt it as a mosque in 1962.
Q126682080: Hızırbey Bath, or Hızırbey Double Bath, is a historic Turkish bath in central Kırklareli. Built as a double bath, it is the oldest and the only surviving hamam in the town centre.
Q127043375: Babaeski Bath, or Fatih Bath, is a historic Turkish bath opposite Fatih Mosque in Babaeski, Kırklareli. Built as a classical Ottoman double bath, only its men's section still stands.
Q127936533: Ferhat Bey Bath, also called Vize Bath or Ağa Bath, is a historic Turkish double bath in the Vize district east of Kırklareli. It is now derelict and out of use.
Q128122389: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha Bath is a historic Turkish double bath in Lüleburgaz, south of Kırklareli. It is now used as the Lüleburgaz municipal council building.
Q131555490: Kale Bath is a historic Turkish bath with men's and women's sections in the Vize district of Kırklareli. It is now derelict and out of use.
Q132089426: Doctor Celepoğlu Mansion, or Celepoğlu House, is a mansion in central Kırklareli built in 1908.
Q133539662: The Karahıdır Monument, also called Karahızır or Four Legs Monument, is an Ottoman-era monument in central Kırklareli.
Q134706663: Doctor Hacı Yanaki Mansion, or Aydın Akkul House, is a late 19th-century mansion in central Kırklareli.
Q6051682: Babaeski Bridge, or Murad IV Bridge, is a historic bridge over the Babaeski stream, a tributary of the Ergene, in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli. It was built in the reign of Murad IV.
Q127060253: Alpullu Bridge, also called Sinanlı or Mehmed Pasha Bridge, is a historic bridge over the Ergene river in the town of Alpullu, Babaeski (Kırklareli).
Q128262145: Sokullu Mehmed Pasha Bridge, or Taşköprü, is a historic bridge over the Lüleburgaz stream in the Lüleburgaz district of Kırklareli. It is thought to have been commissioned from Mimar Sinan by Sokullu Mehmed Pasha in the 16th century.
Q128494288: This Sokullu Mehmed Pasha Bridge, also called Koca Köprü or Taş Köprü, crosses the Yuvalı stream, a tributary of the Ergene, in Büyükkarıştıran, Lüleburgaz (Kırklareli). It is thought to date from the 16th century.
Q124160108: Kadı Ali Fountain is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126365047: Kayyumoğlu Fountain is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126373374: The Prison Fountain (Hapishane Çeşmesi) is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126373402: Kocahıdır Fountain is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126472183: Paşa Fountain, also called Paşa Mosque Fountain or Beyazıt Mosque Fountain, is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q130683946: Karakaş Fountain, or Selim Altıntel Fountain, is a historic fountain in central Kırklareli, built in 1943.
Q130683950: The Covered Fountain (Örtülü Çeşme) is a fountain in the Vize district of Kırklareli.
Q126500932: Hacı Hasan Fountain, or Kara Umur Bey Fountain, is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126538418: Kuru Paşa Fountain is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126539372: Gerdanlı Fountain is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126544788: Salı Yeri Fountain, or Kapan Fountain, is a fountain in central Kırklareli.
Q126722877: The Four-Sided Fountain, also called Meydan or Fatih Fountain, is a fountain in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli.
Q126902168: Avcı Mehmet Fountain, also called Çarşı or Orta Fountain, is a fountain in the Lüleburgaz district of Kırklareli.
Q126902621: Prince Cemaleddin Efendi Fountain, in the garden of Emrullah Efendi Primary School, is a fountain in the Lüleburgaz district of Kırklareli.
Q126902746: The Victory Fountain (Zafer Çeşmesi) is a fountain in the Lüleburgaz district of Kırklareli.
Q126907927: Ferhat Bey Fountain, also called Ferhat Ağa or Cemilzade Mahmut Ağa Fountain, is a fountain in the Vize district of Kırklareli.
Q126910418: Kale Fountain is a fountain in the Vize district of Kırklareli.
Q133683488: This mansion in central Kırklareli, built in 1880, is known as Doctor Kerameas Mansion, Doctor Peterkof's Mansion, the Turkish Hearth Building or the Kırklareli Culture and Art House.
Q127788239: Terzili Village Mosque is a historic Ottoman-era mosque in the village of Terzili, Babaeski (Kırklareli).
Q131390865: The Liman Baba Tomb and open-air prayer place are at the fishing harbour of İğneada, Demirköy (Kırklareli). Built in the Republican era, the site has three concrete structures: the tomb, an ablution fountain and a prayer platform. The turbaned gravestone inside is dated 1795, and the inscription outside 1856.
